plan.contextChunk: This figure shows one undirected weighted graph in which a spanning tree has been picked out by shading. Nine circular vertices carry italic letters: b, c, and d sit across the top, e at the right, f at the lower right, g along the bottom, h at the lower left, a at the left, and i in the middle. Fourteen straight edges join them, each annotated with an integer weight: a-b is 4, b-c is 8, c-d is 7, d-e is 9, a-h is 8, b-h is 11, h-i is 7, h-g is 1, g-i is 6, i-c is 2, c-f is 4, g-f is 2, d-f is 14, and e-f is 10. Eight of those edges, namely a-b, b-c, c-d, d-e, c-i, c-f, h-g, and g-f, are drawn with a broad gray band running behind the line, while the other six remain thin black strokes. The shading is what the reader compares against: it marks an acyclic subset that still reaches every vertex, so the weights along it can be summed and weighed against the heavier unshaded edges it leaves out. The drawing supplies a concrete instance of the wiring problem, in which pins are vertices, possible interconnections are edges, and an edge weight is the amount of wire needed to make that connection.

interactionPlan.concept: A Minimum Spanning Tree connects all vertices in a weighted graph with the lowest possible total edge weight, avoiding cycles, but may not be unique if some edges have identical weights.
elements: 9 circular vertices with light gray fill, black borders, and italic labels a through i
14 thin black edges connecting the vertices: a-b, b-c, c-d, d-e, a-h, b-h, h-i, h-g, g-i, c-i, c-f, g-f, d-f, e-f
14 integer edge weight labels positioned near their respective edges: 4, 8, 7, 9, 8, 11, 7, 1, 6, 2, 4, 2, 14, 10
Thick gray highlight bands drawn behind the edges that form the active Minimum Spanning Tree

interactions.teaches: Clicking an edge reveals its weight and its role: whether it is part of the minimum spanning tree, or if unshaded, the cycle it would form if added.

interactions.label: MST Variant
interactions.teaches: Because edges b-c and a-h have the exact same weight (8), either one can be used to connect the a-b component to the main tree without changing the total cost.

interactions.label: Build Tree
interactions.teaches: The tree is built by considering edges in order of increasing weight and adding them only if they do not form a cycle.

demo_steps.title: What is a Minimum Spanning Tree?
demo_steps.narration: The shaded edges form a tree that connects all 9 vertices without any cycles. Its total edge weight is 37, which is the minimum possible cost to keep the entire graph connected.

demo_steps.title: Building the Tree
demo_steps.narration: A common way to find the MST is to greedily pick the lowest-weight edges first—like g-h (1), c-i (2), and g-f (2)—skipping any that create a closed loop.

demo_steps.title: Excluding Cycles
demo_steps.narration: Click any thin black edge, like h-i (7). Adding it would create a cycle (h-i-c-f-g-h). Since it is the heaviest edge in that cycle, the tree is cheaper without it, so h-i is excluded.

demo_steps.title: Multiple Valid Trees
demo_steps.narration: Toggle the MST Variant. Since edges b-c and a-h both weigh 8, swapping them maintains connectivity without changing the total cost of 37, meaning this graph has two valid Minimum Spanning Trees.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The heaviest edge in any cycle can never belong to a Minimum Spanning Tree, which is why algorithms can build the tree by greedily selecting the lightest available edges.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Planar network diagram with no crossing edges. Approximate layout: 'a' on the far left; 'b', 'c', 'd' along the top; 'h', 'g', 'f' along the bottom; 'i' in the interior between the left and right halves; 'e' on the far right. Place integer weights near the midpoint of each of the 14 thin black edges. The active Minimum Spanning Tree is highlighted by thick, translucent gray bands drawn directly behind its edges. The 'treeVariant' toggle swaps the gray highlight between b-c and a-h. The 'buildState' steps reveal the gray highlights progressively (Empty -> lightest edges 1,2,4 -> Complete).

plan.authoredInteractions:
